```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Article: Dua P, Hawkins E, van der Graaf PH. A Tutorial on Target-Mediated
  Drug Disposition (TMDD) Models. *CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol.*
  2015;4(6):324-337. <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.41> (PMC4505827, open access).
* Supplement: "Berkeley Madonna TMDD model library", a Word document holding the
  authors' runnable Berkeley Madonna code for eight TMDD models, each with a
  complete illustrative parameter set.

Dua 2015 is a tutorial. Its body walks through the TMDD model family, from the
one-compartment Mager and Jusko model through the QE, QSS and Michaelis-Menten
approximations to extensions for multiple targets, competing drugs, receptor-mediated
endocytosis, FcRn recycling and binding outside the central compartment. It
fits no data, and every structure in it is attributed to an earlier paper.

The library takes **two** of the eight supplement models, the two structures it
did not already carry:

| Supplement model | Structure | In this library |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | One-compartment full TMDD | archetype `PK_1cmt_tmdd_full` |
| 2 | Two-compartment full TMDD | structure covered by the archetypes |
| 3 | Two-compartment QE approximation | structure covered by the archetypes |
| 4 | Two-compartment QSS approximation | archetype `PK_2cmt_tmdd_qss` |
| 5 | Two-compartment MM approximation | archetype `PK_2cmt_tmdd_mm` |
| **6** | **Two targets: soluble (QSS) + membrane (MM), after Gibiansky & Gibiansky 2010** | **`Dua_2015_tmdd_multitarget_qss`** |
| **7** | **Full TMDD with FcRn endosomal recycling, after Xiao 2010** | **`Dua_2015_tmdd_fcrn_recycling`** |
| 8 | Two-compartment QSS with denosumab values from Gibiansky 2012 | not taken; the values belong to the Gibiansky 2012 denosumab analysis, which carries the variability and covariate model this transcription drops |

```{r models}
mods <- c("Dua_2015_tmdd_multitarget_qss", "Dua_2015_tmdd_fcrn_recycling")
m6 <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb(mods[1]))
m7 <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb(mods[2]))

tibble::tibble(
  Model = mods,
  `Supplement model` = c(6L, 7L),
  `ODE states` = c(length(m6$state), length(m7$state)),
  Parameters = c(nrow(m6$iniDf), nrow(m7$iniDf))
) |>
  knitr::kable()

# Both are explicit ODE systems. A cl/vc pair would make rxode2 solve them
# analytically and discard the TMDD terms, so confirm that did not happen.
stopifnot(is.null(m6$linCmt), is.null(m7$linCmt))
```

# Population

There is no population. Both parameter sets are illustrative values for a
generic monoclonal antibody, chosen by the authors for teaching. They are not
fitted to data, and the source has no inter-individual variability and no
residual error. Every `ini()` value is therefore `fixed()`, and the residual
error is `fixed(0)` so the models simulate exactly as written.

```{r population}
pop <- readModelDb(mods[1])() |>
  environment() |>
  (\(e) e$population)()
tibble::tibble(Field = names(pop), Value = vapply(pop, \(x) paste(as.character(x), collapse = " "), "")) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

# Units and the dose conversion

Time is days and every concentration is nM.

* **Model 6** works per kg body weight. The supplement doses 10 mg/kg and
  converts it with `Dose = (Dosemg * 1e-3 / MWlig) * 1e9` nmol/kg using
  `MWlig = 150000` Da, then sets `Lc0 = Dose / Vc` with `Vc = 0.04` L/kg. The
  model file is molar (dosing in nmol/kg), so the conversion is applied here.
* **Model 7** has no volume. The supplement gives the dose as the initial
  central concentration `Lc0 = 200` nM, and every transfer between compartments
  is a symmetric first-order rate constant, so all nine states are
  concentrations referenced to the central volume. A dose of `amt = 200` into
  `central` reproduces it.

```{r units}
MW <- 150000 # Supplement Model 6: MWlig = 150000 Da
VC <- 0.04 # Supplement Model 6: Vc = 0.04 L/kg
mgkg_to_nmolkg <- function(mgkg) mgkg * 1e-3 / MW * 1e9

dose6 <- mgkg_to_nmolkg(10)
tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("Model 6 dose (nmol/kg)", "Model 6 Lc0 = Dose/Vc (nM)", "Model 7 Lc0 (nM)"),
  Value = c(dose6, dose6 / VC, 200)
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
stopifnot(abs(dose6 - 66.6667) < 1e-3)
```

# Source trace

Equations are the main text's Eqs V.1-V.6 for Model 6. Model 7 is described only
in prose in the main text ("FcRn recycling"), so its equations come from the
supplement alone. All parameter values come from the supplement.

```{r source-trace-equations}
tibble::tribble(
  ~Model, ~Quantity, ~`Source location`,
  "6", "d/dt Ltot (central), d/dt LT (peripheral1)", "Eqs V.2-V.3; Supplement Model 6 Lctot', Lt'",
  "6", "d/dt Rtot_S (total_target)", "Eq V.4; Supplement Model 6 Rstot'",
  "6", "Free drug LC from the soluble-target QSS quadratic", "Eq V.5; Supplement Model 6 Lc",
  "6", "Rtot_S(0) = R0_S = kin_S/kout_S; LT(0) = 0", "Eq V.6; Supplement Model 6 INIT and kins",
  "6", "Kss_S, Kss_M, Vmax_M = R0_M * kint_M", "Main text 'Multiple targets'; Supplement Model 6",
  "6", "Soluble complex Ps and free soluble target Rs", "Supplement Model 6 'Finding Amount of Free Receptor'",
  "7", "d/dt Lc, Lt, R, Pc, Pt, Le, FcLe, Pe, FcPe", "Supplement Model 7 'Ordinary Differential Equations'",
  "7", "kin = kout * R0; R(0) = R0; all other states 0 except Lc(0) = Lc0", "Supplement Model 7 INIT and rate constants"
) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r source-trace-parameters}
trace_params <- function(ui) {
  ui$iniDf |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(ntheta)) |>
    dplyr::transmute(Parameter = name, Value = signif(ifelse(grepl("^l", name), exp(est), est), 4), Label = label)
}
knitr::kable(trace_params(m6), caption = "Model 6 parameters (all from Supplement Model 6)")
knitr::kable(trace_params(m7), caption = "Model 7 parameters (all from Supplement Model 7)")
```

Every value in both tables appears verbatim in the supplement; the in-file
comment on each `ini()` line names the supplement variable it came from
(`kpt` is the library's `k12`, `ktp` its `k21`, `kout` its `kdeg`, and `kep`
its `kint`).

## Units of every ODE term

| Model | State | Units | Every term reduces to |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | `central` (total drug amount) | nmol/kg | `(L/kg) x (1/day) x nM` = nmol/kg/day |
| 6 | `peripheral1` (tissue drug amount, = Lt x Vc) | nmol/kg | `(1/day) x (L/kg) x nM` or `(1/day) x nmol/kg` |
| 6 | `total_target` | nM | `nM/day` (`ksyn`) or `(1/day) x nM` |
| 7 | all nine states | nM | `(1/day) x nM`, or `(1/(nM day)) x nM x nM` for binding |

The Model 6 Michaelis-Menten term `Vmax_M * Lc / (Kss_M + Lc)` has
`Vmax_M = R0_M * kint_M` in nM/day, so it is a concentration rate and is
multiplied by `Vc` along with the other central terms.

# Model 6: soluble plus membrane target

## Drug-free steady state

With no drug, the soluble target must hold at its baseline `Rs0 = 0.00657` nM
indefinitely, because `kins = kouts * Rs0`.

```{r m6-steady}
tight <- list(rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6)
ev0 <- rxode2::et(seq(0, 100, by = 1))
s0 <- do.call(rxode2::rxSolve, c(list(m6, ev0, returnType = "data.frame"), tight))
stopifnot(max(abs(s0$total_target / 0.00657 - 1)) < 1e-8, max(abs(s0$central)) == 0)
```

## Single 10 mg/kg dose (Supplement Model 6 regimen)

The supplement simulates one 10 mg/kg i.v. bolus for 360 days.

```{r m6-sim}
grid6 <- sort(unique(c(0, exp(seq(log(1e-4), log(360), length.out = 2500)))))
ev6 <- rxode2::et(amt = dose6, cmt = "central") |> rxode2::et(grid6)
s6 <- do.call(rxode2::rxSolve, c(list(m6, ev6, returnType = "data.frame"), tight))

s6 |>
  dplyr::select(time, `Free drug Lc` = Cc, `Total drug Ltot` = ctot, `Total soluble target` = total_target) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "Concentration (nM)", title = "Supplement Model 6, 10 mg/kg i.v.")
```

## Removing the membrane target reduces Model 6 to the library's QSS archetype

With the membrane target set to (numerically) zero, Model 6 is exactly the
two-compartment QSS TMDD model (Supplement Model 4). The library already ships
that structure as `PK_2cmt_tmdd_qss`, written independently with a CL/V
parameterisation and an amount-based peripheral compartment. Mapping the
Model 6 constants onto it (`CL = kel * Vc`, `Q = kpt * Vc`, `Vp = Vc * kpt/ktp`)
must give the same total-drug profile. This checks the central, peripheral and
soluble-target equations of Model 6 against a second, separately written
implementation.

```{r m6-archetype, message = FALSE}
s6_nomem <- do.call(
  rxode2::rxSolve,
  c(list(m6, ev6, params = c(lrtot_mem = log(1e-15)), returnType = "data.frame"), tight)
)

kss <- (169 + 0.170) / 30.2 # Supplement Model 4/6: Kss = (koff + kep)/kon
arch <- readModelDb("PK_2cmt_tmdd_qss") |>
  rxode2::zeroRe() |>
  rxode2::ini(
    lcl = log(0.046 * VC), lvc = log(VC), lvp = log(VC * 0.902 / 0.725), lq = log(0.902 * VC),
    lT0 = log(0.00657), lkdeg = log(17.3), lkint = log(0.170), lkss = log(kss)
  )
s_arch <- do.call(rxode2::rxSolve, c(list(arch, ev6, returnType = "data.frame"), tight))

rel_arch <- max(abs(s_arch$Cc / s6_nomem$ctot - 1))
rel_arch
stopifnot(nrow(s_arch) == nrow(s6_nomem), rel_arch < 1e-6)
```

## Drug mass balance

Drug leaves the body only through linear elimination of free drug, elimination
of the soluble complex and the membrane-target Michaelis-Menten term, so the
dose must equal the drug still in the body plus the cumulative eliminated flux.
The flux is integrated with the trapezoidal rule on the dense log grid, which
limits the closure to about 1e-5 (measured 6e-6).

```{r m6-massbalance}
flux6 <- with(s6, VC * (0.046 * Cc + total_target * 0.170 * Cc / (kss + Cc) +
  0.002 * 0.170 * Cc / ((169 + 0.170) / 30.2 + Cc)))
cum6 <- c(0, cumsum(diff(s6$time) * (head(flux6, -1) + tail(flux6, -1)) / 2))
closure6 <- (s6$central + s6$peripheral1 + cum6) / dose6 - 1
max(abs(closure6))
stopifnot(max(abs(closure6)) < 1e-4)
```

## How much the membrane target contributes

The membrane term is a saturable extra elimination pathway, so removing it can
only raise exposure, and its share of elimination grows as the dose falls and
free drug approaches `Kss_M` (5.6 nM). With the tutorial's illustrative values
the pathway is small at every dose: the total membrane target is only
`Rm0 = 0.002` nM, against free-drug concentrations of tens to thousands of nM.

```{r m6-doses}
auc_free <- function(sim) sum(diff(sim$time) * (head(sim$Cc, -1) + tail(sim$Cc, -1)) / 2)
dose_tab <- lapply(c(0.01, 0.1, 1, 10), function(d) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = mgkg_to_nmolkg(d), cmt = "central") |> rxode2::et(grid6)
  with_m <- do.call(rxode2::rxSolve, c(list(m6, ev, returnType = "data.frame"), tight))
  no_m <- do.call(rxode2::rxSolve, c(list(m6, ev, params = c(lrtot_mem = log(1e-15)), returnType = "data.frame"), tight))
  tibble::tibble(
    `Dose (mg/kg)` = d,
    `Free-drug AUC with membrane target (nM day)` = auc_free(with_m),
    `Free-drug AUC without (nM day)` = auc_free(no_m)
  )
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows() |>
  dplyr::mutate(`Exposure lost to membrane target (%)` = 100 * (1 - `Free-drug AUC with membrane target (nM day)` / `Free-drug AUC without (nM day)`))
knitr::kable(dose_tab, digits = 3)
lost <- dose_tab$`Exposure lost to membrane target (%)`
stopifnot(
  all(dose_tab$`Free-drug AUC with membrane target (nM day)` < dose_tab$`Free-drug AUC without (nM day)`),
  lost[1] > lost[4]
)
```

The membrane target removes `r signif(lost[1], 2)`% of free-drug exposure at
0.01 mg/kg and `r signif(lost[4], 2)`% at 10 mg/kg. Free-drug AUC is close to
dose-proportional across the whole range. With these values, neither target is
abundant enough to give the nonlinear profile TMDD is known for; raise `Rm0` or
`Rs0` to see it.

## The supplement's soluble-complex formula

The supplement computes the soluble complex as
`Ps = Lctot - Lc - Rm0 * Lc / (Kssm + Lc)`, subtracting the membrane-bound drug
from total drug. But `Lc` comes from the soluble-target quadratic, which solves
`Lctot = Lc + Rstot * Lc / (Ksss + Lc)` and so does not include membrane-bound
drug in `Lctot`. The two definitions disagree by exactly the membrane-bound
term, `Rm0 * Lc / (Kssm + Lc)`. The model file keeps the printed form
(`complex_sol`, `target_sol`) and adds the QSS-consistent form
(`complex_sol_qss`, `target_sol_qss`). The identity below also confirms that
the quadratic is solved correctly at every time point.

```{r m6-complex}
bias <- with(s6, (complex_sol_qss - complex_sol) - 0.002 * Cc / ((169 + 0.170) / 30.2 + Cc))
max(abs(bias))
stopifnot(max(abs(bias)) < 1e-9)

s6 |>
  dplyr::select(time, `As printed (target_sol)` = target_sol, `QSS-consistent (target_sol_qss)` = target_sol_qss) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = name)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "Free soluble target (nM)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

While drug is in excess the printed form understates the bound soluble target
by about `Rm0 = 0.002` nM. The baseline is only 0.00657 nM, so the printed
free soluble target sits near 0.002 nM where the QSS relation puts it close to
zero. Use `target_sol_qss` for target-suppression questions.

# Model 7: full TMDD with FcRn recycling

## Drug-free steady state

```{r m7-steady}
s7_0 <- do.call(rxode2::rxSolve, c(list(m7, ev0, returnType = "data.frame"), tight))
stopifnot(max(abs(s7_0$target / 0.03 - 1)) < 1e-8, max(abs(s7_0$central)) == 0)
```

## Single dose, Lc0 = 200 nM (Supplement Model 7 regimen)

The supplement simulates 28 days.

```{r m7-sim}
grid7 <- sort(unique(c(0, seq(0, 28, by = 0.005))))
ev7 <- rxode2::et(amt = 200, cmt = "central") |> rxode2::et(grid7)
s7 <- do.call(rxode2::rxSolve, c(list(m7, ev7, returnType = "data.frame"), tight))

s7 |>
  dplyr::select(
    time,
    `Free drug, central` = central, `Free drug, tissue` = peripheral1,
    `Free target` = target, `Complex, central` = complex,
    `Endosomal drug, free` = endosome, `Endosomal drug, FcRn-bound` = endosome_fcrn,
    `Endosomal complex, free` = complex_endosome, `Endosomal complex, FcRn-bound` = complex_endosome_fcrn
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "Concentration (nM)", title = "Supplement Model 7, Lc0 = 200 nM")
```

## Drug mass balance

Summing the eight drug-containing equations, every binding, transfer, uptake and
recycling term cancels and only four elimination terms remain:
`kelc * Lc + kepc * Pc + kele * Le + kele * Pe`. So the 200 nM dose must equal
the drug left in the eight states plus the integrated elimination.

```{r m7-massbalance}
drug7 <- with(s7, central + peripheral1 + complex + complex_peripheral1 +
  endosome + endosome_fcrn + complex_endosome + complex_endosome_fcrn)
flux7 <- with(s7, 0.024 * central + 0.201 * complex + 0.024 * endosome + 0.024 * complex_endosome)
cum7 <- c(0, cumsum(diff(s7$time) * (head(flux7, -1) + tail(flux7, -1)) / 2))
closure7 <- (drug7 + cum7) / 200 - 1
max(abs(closure7))
stopifnot(max(abs(closure7)) < 1e-6) # measured 4e-8
```

## Switching off distribution and endosomal uptake reduces Model 7 to the one-compartment full TMDD archetype

With `kup` and `kpt` set to (numerically) zero, no drug reaches the tissue or the
endosome, and Model 7 is exactly the one-compartment full TMDD model (Supplement
Model 1, whose binding constants Model 7 reuses). The library ships that
structure as `PK_1cmt_tmdd_full`. With `Vc = 1` L and the dose as 200 mg its
central amount equals the Model 7 concentration, so the two free-drug profiles
must coincide.

```{r m7-archetype, message = FALSE}
s7_red <- do.call(
  rxode2::rxSolve,
  c(list(m7, ev7, params = c(lkup = log(1e-15), lk12 = log(1e-15)), returnType = "data.frame"), tight)
)
arch1 <- readModelDb("PK_1cmt_tmdd_full") |>
  rxode2::zeroRe() |>
  rxode2::ini(
    lcl = log(0.024), lvc = log(1), lT0 = log(0.03), lkdeg = log(0.823),
    lkint = log(0.201), lkon = log(0.592), lkoff = log(0.9)
  )
s_arch1 <- do.call(rxode2::rxSolve, c(list(arch1, ev7, returnType = "data.frame"), tight))

rel_arch1 <- max(abs(s_arch1$Cc / s7_red$Cc - 1))
rel_arch1
stopifnot(nrow(s_arch1) == nrow(s7_red), rel_arch1 < 1e-6)
```

## What FcRn recycling does to exposure

Without FcRn, drug taken up into the endosome is lost: it is eliminated there at
`kele` and never returns. With FcRn, the bound fraction is recycled to the
central compartment, so central exposure can only be higher.

```{r m7-fcrn}
s7_nofc <- do.call(
  rxode2::rxSolve,
  c(list(m7, ev7, params = c(lrtot_fcrn = log(1e-15)), returnType = "data.frame"), tight)
)
cmp7 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(s7, scenario = "FcRn 0.05 nM (Supplement Model 7)"),
  dplyr::mutate(s7_nofc, scenario = "No FcRn")
)
ggplot(cmp7, aes(time, Cc, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "Free drug, central (nM)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

auc7 <- c(fcrn = auc_free(s7), nofcrn = auc_free(s7_nofc))
auc7
stopifnot(auc7[["fcrn"]] > auc7[["nofcrn"]])
```

## PKNCA on the free-drug profiles

The paper reports no NCA, so there is no published table to compare against.
PKNCA is run here on the deterministic free-drug profiles as a descriptive
summary, grouped by model and scenario. Model 7 is simulated over the supplement's 28-day
horizon, so a large part of its `aucinf.obs` is extrapolated.

```{r pknca, message = FALSE}
conc_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::transmute(s6, id = 1L, treatment = "Model 6, 10 mg/kg", time, Cc),
  dplyr::transmute(s7, id = 2L, treatment = "Model 7, FcRn", time, Cc),
  dplyr::transmute(s7_nofc, id = 3L, treatment = "Model 7, no FcRn", time, Cc)
) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc))
dose_nca <- tibble::tibble(
  id = 1:3, time = 0,
  treatment = c("Model 6, 10 mg/kg", "Model 7, FcRn", "Model 7, no FcRn"),
  amt = c(dose6, 200, 200)
)
o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, amt ~ time | treatment + id, route = "intravascular")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals))
summary(nca) |> knitr::kable()
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Only two of the eight supplement models are in the library.** Models 1-5
  repeat structures the library already carries as TMDD archetypes, and Model 8
  transcribes the Gibiansky 2012 denosumab estimates without that analysis's
  variability and covariate model, so it is best taken from the primary paper.
* **Illustrative parameters, not estimates.** Neither model is fitted to data.
  Use them to explore model behaviour, not to predict any real antibody.
* **Model 6 is the i.v. form.** Main-text Eqs V.1 and V.3 also carry a
  subcutaneous depot (`dLD/dt = -ka*LD`, `LD(0) = D1`). Supplement Model 6 is
  i.v.-only and no absorption rate constant is printed anywhere, so no depot is
  included. (The input term of Eq V.3 is typeset `kf LD`; with the depot of
  Eq V.1 it is the absorption term.)
* **Model 6 soluble-complex formula.** The printed `Ps` is inconsistent with the
  quadratic that defines `Lc`, by exactly the membrane-bound drug. Both forms are
  reported; see the section above.
* **Model 7 `kepe` is unused.** The supplement lists `kepe = 0.201` 1/day
  ("elimination of complex from endosome compartment"), but its `Pe` equation
  eliminates endosomal complex with `kele = 0.024` 1/day, the same rate as
  endosomal free drug. The model file follows the equation. The main text
  describes the Xiao model as having equal elimination rates for drug and
  complex (`ke(LC) = ke(PC)`); the supplement applies that equality only in the
  endosome, while in the central compartment it keeps `kelc = 0.024` and
  `kepc = 0.201` 1/day. `kepe` is not carried in `ini()` because no equation
  uses it.
* **Model 7 FcRn is constant, and with these values that assumption is
  stretched.** Following Xiao 2010, the tutorial holds FcRn fixed at
  `Fc0 = 0.05` nM rather than tracking free FcRn. With the illustrative dose, the
  FcRn-bound drug pool reaches
  `r signif(max(s7$endosome_fcrn + s7$complex_endosome_fcrn), 3)` nM, well above
  the stated FcRn concentration. A model that conserved FcRn would saturate the
  recycling pathway; this one does not. This is a property of the published
  model, reproduced as written.
* **Model 7 has no volume.** Doses are concentrations (nM). To dose an amount,
  divide it by a central volume of your choosing; none is printed for Model 7.
* **No variability or residual error.** `propSd` is `fixed(0)` in both files.
* **Integrator.** The supplement integrates with fourth-order Runge-Kutta at
  `DT = 0.01` day. Here the models are solved with LSODA at tight tolerances.
